columnPool.label: Route: Swanline
columnPool.display: Is part of the Swanline route
columnPool.hint: The local stopping service on the South Wales Main Line between Cardiff Central and Swansea, calling at Pyle, Port Talbot, Baglan, Briton Ferry, Skewen and Llansamlet - the slower alternative to the fast Cardiff-Swansea trains.

columnPool.label: Route: Central Wales Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Central Wales Line route
columnPool.hint: The long single-track 'Heart of Wales' route south from Craven Arms through Knighton, Llandrindod Wells, Llandovery and Llandeilo to Llanelli and Swansea - same route as the Heart of Wales Line, just an older name.

columnPool.label: Route: Heart of Wales Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Heart of Wales Line route
columnPool.hint: The long single-track route south from Craven Arms through Knighton, Llandrindod Wells, Llandovery and Llandeilo to Llanelli and Swansea - also called the Central Wales Line.

columnPool.label: Route: Vale of Glamorgan Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Vale of Glamorgan Line route
columnPool.hint: The line looping south of the Cardiff-Bridgend main line via Barry, Rhoose Cardiff Airport and Llantwit Major - reopened to passengers in 2005 after over 40 years closed.

columnPool.label: Route: Coryton Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Coryton Line route
columnPool.hint: The short suburban branch north from Cardiff Queen Street through Heath, Birchgrove, Rhiwbina and Whitchurch to Coryton - not one of the longer Valley lines further out.

columnPool.label: Route: Merthyr Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Merthyr Line route
columnPool.hint: The Valley line north from Cardiff via Abercynon to Merthyr Tydfil - shares its southern half with the Aberdare Line, which splits off at Abercynon.

columnPool.label: Route: Treherbert Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Treherbert Line route
columnPool.hint: The Rhondda Valley line from Cardiff via Pontypridd, Porth and Tonypandy to Treherbert at the head of the valley.

columnPool.label: Route: Aberdare Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Aberdare Line route
columnPool.hint: The Valley line north from Cardiff via Abercynon to Aberdare - shares its southern half with the Merthyr Line, which splits off at Abercynon.

columnPool.label: Route: Ebbw Valley Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Ebbw Valley Line route
columnPool.hint: The reopened branch up the Ebbw Valley from Newport (or Cardiff Central) through Risca, Crosskeys and Newbridge to Ebbw Vale Town - closed to passengers for 46 years before reopening in 2008.

columnPool.label: Route: Cardiff Bay Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Cardiff Bay Line route
columnPool.hint: The short shuttle branch from Cardiff Queen Street down to Cardiff Bay, serving the regenerated docks and Senedd area - also called the Butetown Branch Line.

columnPool.label: Route: Severn Beach Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Severn Beach Line route
columnPool.hint: The scenic Bristol suburban branch from Temple Meads through Clifton Down, Sea Mills and Avonmouth to the small resort of Severn Beach on the Severn Estuary.

columnPool.label: Route: Great Western Main Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Great Western Main Line route
columnPool.hint: The core route from London Paddington to Bristol and beyond, via Reading, Swindon and Bath Spa - the trunk line South Wales services join at Bristol Parkway or Bristol Temple Meads.

columnPool.label: Route: City Line (Cardiff)
columnPool.display: Is part of the City Line (Cardiff) route
columnPool.hint: The short Cardiff line linking Radyr to Cardiff Central/Queen Street via Danescourt, Fairwater, Waun-Gron Park and Ninian Park - also used as a diversion route for the Valley lines.

columnPool.label: Route: Gloucester to Newport Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Gloucester to Newport Line route
columnPool.hint: The route hugging the English side of the Severn Estuary from Newport through Chepstow and Lydney up to Gloucester - the diversionary route when the Severn Tunnel is closed.

columnPool.label: Route: Marches Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Marches Line route
columnPool.hint: The long cross-border route from Newport via Abergavenny and Hereford to Shrewsbury, continuing to Crewe or via Wrexham to Chester - same route as the North & West Line, just an older name. Not the Heart of Wales branch that splits off at Craven Arms.
